correctness.rationale: Proved exact Stern triple identity by strong induction; finite irreducible aperiodic primitive-residue Markov chain uniformly mixes; conditioned terminal bits have geometric frequency independently of mixed residue pair; dyadic cylinder decomposition yields full natural densities; solution of 2bt=a+c-b modulo m gives closed formula incl q=1 and composite cases. Finite checks independently replayed: 200000 identity cases; mass normalization, pair marginals and reachability for m=2..12; observed distribution for m=3,4,6,7 in a full 65536-index row. Infinite theorem proved analytically, not inferred from finite tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest broad results give pair uniformity or distributions of normal functions of a pair; s(n+2) depends on ν2(n+1) and is not such a function. This work conditions terminal suffixes and sums a geometric mixture. No inspected theorem already states or directly supplies the complete triple support and weights.

originality.rationale: Reznick 2006/2008 establishes primitive-pair equidistribution but not the third term law. Northshield 2022 gives normal functions of the first two terms but does not cover index-dependent third term. Stanley 2020 proposes k-consecutive Stern congruences as a further problem; this resolves k=3 with an exact all-modulus formula. Neither source inspections nor targeted research-result/literature searches identified prior equivalent triple formula; absolute priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An unindexed or less directly titled prior result could already give the triple law, despite no such result in inspected relevant primary texts.
The explicit triple formula might be derivable through a general digital-transducer theorem not inspected here; publication priority is not absolute.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Stanley (2020) explicitly motivates congruence patterns on k consecutive Stern terms. The k=3 answer provides an exact natural density for every triple and every modulus, a complete support criterion, an explicit nonuniform conditional distribution, and a sharp contrast with known pair equidistribution. This is a complete natural classification rather than an arbitrary finite numerical slice; it makes no k>=4 claim.
